bullets.title: Futures recover: S&P +0.75%, SOXX +3.2% as semis rally on INTC upgrade and CPI relief
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures trade up 0.75% to 7333 premarket with 10-year yields +3bps to 4.52%. The semiconductor ETF SOXX is up 3.23% after BofA upgraded INTC to Buy (from Underperform, PT $135/$96) citing improved CPU outlook, while May core CPI came in at 0.208% vs. 0.27% JPM estimate, giving relief to rate-sensitive baskets. RTY leads indices up ~1.4% on non-tech cyclical rotation.

bullets.title: ORCL -9% on capex shock: $70B net cash FY27 guidance and $20B equity raise overshadow beat
bullets.body: Oracle beat F4Q26 EPS ($2.11 vs $1.96) and revenue ($19.18B), but the stock fell 8-10% on FY27 net cash capex guidance of ~$70B (gross $90-95B) and plans to raise $40B in FY27 ($20B equity ATM + $20B debt). Cloud revenue missed ($9.91B vs $10.0B expected) and FY27 gross margins face pressure from capacity ramps, though backlog hit a record $638B (+$85B q/q). OCI growth guided to accelerate to ~120% in 1Q FY27. UBS and Citi maintain Buy; stock seen as overly punished on peak-capex concerns.

bullets.title: Memory supercycle: Wolfe raises MU PT to $1,250 on DRAM pricing up 35% q/q and supply constrained through CY28
bullets.body: Wolfe raises MU CY27 revenue estimate to $226B (vs street $186B) and EPS to $135 (vs street $107), citing DRAM ASP rising 35% q/q in C2Q after +75% in 1Q, with another +15% forecast for 3Q. HBM pricing expected to rise 40% in CY27 driven by HBM4/4E adoption; LTAs with penalty clauses set a new pricing precedent. Supply constrained by cleanroom capacity through CY27-CY28. MU trades at ~7x CY27 EPS vs. 10x historical average.

bullets.title: HDD pricing cycle accelerating: JPM raises STX PT to $920 and WDC PT to $650 on 90%+ FY27 EPS growth
bullets.body: JPM's Samik Chatterjee forecasts low-to-mid single-digit sequential HDD price increases accelerating to +10-11% YoY in FY27 for both WDC and STX. AI workloads (training, inferencing, robotics) driving exabyte growth at 25%+ pace; hyperscalers signing LTAs extending to 2032. Neither company adding unit capacity, supporting durable pricing cycle. FY27 gross margins modeled at 58.6% for WDC and 54.5% for STX; 90%+ EPS growth in FY27.

bullets.title: Optical pullback overdone: JPM reiterates OW on COHR and LITE at sub-1x PEG with CPO ramp on track
bullets.body: JPM pushes back on the ~20% pullback in optical names as overblown. NVDA CPO ramp tracking better than expected; LITE reports CPO-supported switch mix now >50% vs. 40-50% prior. Both COHR and LITE trade at ~25x CY28 consensus for 40%+ EPS growth. DoD addition of Chinese optical suppliers (Innolight, Eoptolink) to Pentagon list could accelerate de-risking toward U.S. verticals. TSMC leading-edge fab utilization at 110-120% with no relief until 2027-2028.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex estimates too conservative: GS sees $1.1-1.4T in 2027 vs. consensus $920B
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs argues consensus 2027 hyperscaler capex estimates (~$920B) are too conservative and could reach $1.1-1.4T. ORCL's FY27 capex guidance ($90-95B gross) underscores the magnitude of AI infrastructure buildout. AI infrastructure stocks now trade at a median 26x P/E (highest since ChatGPT launch), signaling valuation expansion and potential volatility ahead. Record 2026 equity issuance (~$1T in buybacks) not expected to disrupt market.

bullets.title: OpenAI token price war: drastic cuts anticipated, bearish for AI vendor ARR, bullish for adoption
bullets.body: The WSJ and multiple sell-side desks report OpenAI is weighing significant token price cuts to compete with Anthropic for enterprise customers. Lower pricing expected to drive higher adoption but risks near-term ARR updates for exposed software vendors. The LLM Token Expenditure Index has stalled, with usage migrating toward open-source models. AI infrastructure median P/E at 26x signals market is pricing in aggressive growth that may prove volatile if pricing pressure accelerates.

bullets.title: Iran-Hormuz escalation: Strait of Hormuz traffic dropped to zero; calibrated conflict unlikely to broaden
bullets.body: The Strait of Hormuz reportedly saw traffic drop to zero following the latest round of US-Iran strikes; Iran's IRGC warned against vessels transiting the Gulf. Despite escalating frequency of strikes (US Tomahawks, Iranian ballistic missiles into Kuwait/Bahrain/Jordan), analysis suggests both sides remain calibrated and a general deal framework is possible. Over 100 days in, global oil markets have absorbed the supply disruption via demand loss, dark-vessel flows (~2mn bbl/day), and inventory releases. WTI ~$89-90, with Brent jumping $2 on latest escalation. The ECB is expected to raise rates 25bps today partly in response to the Iran-driven energy shock pushing Eurozone inflation above target.

bullets.title: May CPI: core soft at 0.21% MoM, but embedded services inflation and energy PPI surge complicate Fed path
bullets.body: May core CPI printed 0.208% MoM (2.9% YoY), below JPM's 0.27% estimate, providing near-term relief. However, core services inflation shows signs of becoming embedded, and energy PPI has surged 21.3% cumulatively since January. PPI expected at 0.7% headline/0.6% core today. JPM and Hedgeye both flag Quad 4-like macro slowdown risk while the Fed stays on hold. The ECB is hiking 25bps today, and the BoJ is expected to tighten 25bps next week to 1.00%.

bullets.title: Retail tech selling hit all-time records; rotation into defensives and non-tech cyclicals
bullets.body: JPM reports retail investors recorded their heaviest tech ETF selling on record (-3.7z) with SOXL, SMH, IGV leading outflows; most-sold names included ARM (-7.0z), MRVL (-6.9z), AMD (-3.0z), DELL (-4.0z), MU (-3.2z). Tech stocks saw $10.8B in outflows last week (largest ever per one data point). Rotation moved into Consumer Staples and Healthcare, with defensive sectors outperforming tech by 11-12%. NVDA and TSLA were notable exceptions, returning to top retail buy lists.

bullets.title: AI momentum unwind: Jefferies notes 86% S&P beat rate but ex-AI earnings revisions flat; AI stocks at 26x median P/E
bullets.body: Jefferies flags recent correction as a momentum unwind in crowded AI trades triggered by modest catalysts, not a fundamental shift. US 1Q26 results set a record 86% beat rate, with AI driving ~80% of S&P 500 gains on ~39% EPS CAGR. Ex-AI earnings revisions remain flat, explaining weak broader-market performance. Near-term leadership may broaden toward value, yield, and lower-volatility exposures; caution warranted on momentum stocks without strong earnings support.

bullets.title: Goldman upgrades MSCI EM to 2000 target; Korea and Taiwan positioned as AI plays with overweight conviction
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs upgraded its MSCI EM 12-month target to 2000, driven by robust AI-exposed earnings growth in North Asian markets. Prime brokerage flows show broadening hedge fund demand into China, Japan, and Brazil. Korea and Taiwan are overweight as premier AI semiconductor plays. South Korea's June 1-10 semiconductor exports surged 206% YoY while the KOSPI saw historic liquidation pressure (put/call ratio at GFC highs) before recovering to flat on the session.

bullets.title: China InP export controls threaten AI photonic buildout; US officials pressing Beijing
bullets.body: Reuters confirms US officials have visited China multiple times urging resolution of indium phosphide (InP) export delays, which are constraining US photonic chip manufacturers critical for AI data center interconnects. China's control over InP supply is seen as a strategic chokepoint; DoD has added Chinese optical suppliers Innolight and Eoptolink to the Pentagon list, potentially accelerating reshoring toward COHR and LITE.

bullets.title: KKR launches $10B Helix Digital data center JV with NVDA and Vistra as anchor partners
bullets.body: KKR, Kuwait Investment Authority, NVIDIA, and Vistra announced Helix Digital Infrastructure with $10B+ in committed capital. NVIDIA serves as strategic partner for AI factory-aligned infrastructure; Vistra is the preferred power provider. Former AWS CEO Adam Selipsky leads the entity. This underscores the ongoing institutional capital mobilization into AI data center power and compute infrastructure.

bullets.title: SaaS multiples compressing: IGV -13.2% YTD vs. S&P +8.7%; NOW flagged for RIF
bullets.body: Wolfe Research reports the All-SaaS index trades at 5.2x FY+2 EV/Sales, with multiples down 2.63% week-over-week. IGV has returned -13.2% YTD vs. S&P 500 +8.7%. NOW is undergoing a reduction in force (RIF). ADBE reports after the close tonight with 33% YTD decline driven by AI disruption concerns; CEO transition is the primary investor focus. FY26 ARR growth guidance of 10.2% is unlikely to see FY27 raises.

bullets.title: TSMC CoPoS advanced packaging pulled in from 2029 to 2028; leading-edge fabs at 110-120% utilization
bullets.body: TSMC accelerated its CoPoS (Co-Package-on-Substrate) advanced packaging timeline by one year to 2028. TSMC's leading-edge nodes (N3 and below) are running at 110-120% utilization with no relief expected until 2027/early 2028. TSMC is expected to revise up 2026 revenue guidance to 35%+ YoY, with N3/below price hike discussions beginning in 2Q26 for 2027 pricing. Amkor is investing $650M in South Korea packaging expansion driven by a TSMC order surge.

bullets.title: MSFT Xbox layoffs and META Manus unwind: two big-tech headline risks beyond earnings
bullets.body: Microsoft's Xbox division is planning major layoffs post-June 30 fiscal year-end after Xbox revenue declined nearly $500M annually despite $20B+ in content/hardware investment (profit margins down to 3%). Separately, Meta has been forced to unwind its $2B Manus AI acquisition after China's NDRC blocked it on security review grounds; Meta has ceased data sharing with Manus and is 'sunsetting' the unit. Microsoft is also restricting internal use of Claude Fable over data-retention concerns.

bullets.title: ECB hiking to 2.25% today; BoJ to 1.00% next week as energy shock drives inflation above targets
bullets.body: The ECB is expected to deliver its first rate hike since 2023 today, bringing its policy rate to 2.25%, with three hikes projected for the year. The BoJ is set to hike 25bps next Tuesday to 1.00%, though analysts note BoJ policy remains the lowest among developed markets and well below Japan's nominal GDP growth, creating pressure for faster tightening. Weak yen and surging JGB yields (40-year at 3.765%) are amplifying BoJ urgency.

bullets.title: Google zero-click searches at 68%; AI Overviews cut CTR by 60%—structural pressure on RDDT and web publishers
bullets.body: Google zero-click searches reached 68% in the first four months of 2026 (up from 60% in 2024), with AI Overviews present on 20%+ of searches and reducing click-through rates by nearly 60%. This is structural negative pressure on ad-supported content platforms and search-dependent publishers. Google Gemini is now the clear winner for consumer AI use cases (3.65 avg vote vs. Claude 1.71 and ChatGPT 1.65).

bullets.title: Russell 2000 outperforming YTD (+14.2% vs S&P 500 +8.1%); non-tech cyclical rotation supporting small caps
bullets.body: The Russell 2000 is up 14.2% YTD vs. the S&P 500's 8.1% gain, outperforming by 6+ percentage points. On June 10, RTY fell only 1.1% vs. the S&P 500's 1.6% decline. 1Q26 aggregate Russell 2000 earnings came in 12.9% below expectations (44.7% ex-financials), while revenues beat by 2.6%. Non-tech cyclical rotation is supporting the relative outperformance.
